ops.title: daemonkit revisit: the client already holds the peercred pid — cross-check it against Health.PID
ops.body:
Identified 2026-08-04 by a consumer (cc-pool statusapp) while closing a
process-identity finding. Recorded as a daemonkit-revisit item; daemonkit was
frozen for the v0.21 flag day, so nothing was changed.

## The gap

`Health.PID` is the serving daemon's **self-report**, not a verified fact:
`serve.go:215` fills `wire.Serving{PID: os.Getpid(), ...}`, carried at
`internal/wire/health.go:43` and decoded at `health.go:83`.

Separately, `authorizeServer` **kernel-verifies** the socket peer via
LOCAL_PEERCRED (`control.go:125,156`) — so the client already holds a
trustworthy pid for the process it is talking to, at the moment it is talking
to it.

Nothing cross-checks the two. A serving process could report a PID other than
its own and the client would believe it.

## Why it does not bite today

With `ServingSigned`, only the genuine installed binary can hold the session,
and the genuine binary reports `os.Getpid()` faithfully. Under the weaker
`ServingSameUser()` floor a same-UID process could misreport — but a same-UID
attacker is already the user, which is the floor that lane accepts by design.
So this is defense-in-depth, not a live hole.

## The cheap structural fix

Have the client compare `Health.PID` against the peercred pid it already
obtained during `authorizeServer`, and refuse on mismatch. No new syscall, no
new round trip, no protocol change — the data is already in hand on both sides
of the comparison. It converts "the daemon says it is pid N" into "the kernel
says this socket belongs to pid N, and the daemon agrees."

That would let a consumer trust `Health.PID` for correlation without building
its own bracket, which is what cc-pool had to do (see the three-mechanism
comment in `internal/statusapp/deployment.go`: session binds answer to identity,
bracket pins the process instance, WaitReady proves live-and-ready).

Companion to note 5f94de3 (comparing Serving values with `==` panics) — both
are daemonkit API sharp edges found by consumers during the v0.21 migration.
